_prereg: PAN-33 local code benchmark, frozen 2026-10-09 BEFORE any model is run on it.
Question: which locally runnable model writes code that passes hidden tests, at what speed, on M2's 16 GB card --
the choice the program faces for a code-mutation operator. The 15-probe smoke test could not rank models
(13/15 has a 95 percent interval of about 0.62-0.96); n = 164 can separate pass rates about 0.1 apart.
CAVEAT stated in advance: HumanEval (2021) is very likely in every model's training data; read RANKS and speeds,
not absolute capability. No claim about reasoning is made from this set.

protocol.runtime: Ollama 0.35.0 on M2, temperature 0, seed 1, num_ctx = budget + 1024
protocol.prompt: the HumanEval prompt followed by: Complete the function above. Reply with ONLY one Python code block (```python ... ```) containing the complete function, including the signature. No explanation, no tests.
protocol.extraction: the last ```python block; if none, the whole response
protocol.execution: imports from the prompt + extracted code + the EvalPlus test + check(entry_point), in a fresh `python -I` subprocess in a temp dir, 60 s timeout; pass = exit 0 and the sentinel printed
protocol.metric: pass@1 (greedy), with a Wilson 95 percent interval; median tokens/s; truncations counted

controls.POSITIVE: every canonical solution passes its own tests (164/164), else the harness is broken and NO model result is reported
controls.CHEAT: a stub body (`pass`, returns None) passes at most 5 of 164 (problems whose tests expect None are possible), else the tests are not discriminating
controls.NEGATIVE: the prompt alone (signature + docstring, no body) passes at most 5 of 164

comparison_rule: two configurations differ only if their Wilson 95 percent intervals do not overlap; otherwise reported as not separable

amendments.change: exclude HumanEval/32 (find_zero); n = 163; POSITIVE control becomes 163/163
amendments.evidence: the controls run (roles/Pan/reports/codebench/CONTROLS_*.json) gave canonical 163/164; the only failure is HumanEval/32, whose EvalPlus test asserts `_poly(*candidate(*inp), inp) <= 0.0001`: it star-unpacks the candidate's return value, a float, so every candidate -- the canonical solution included -- raises TypeError ('Value after * must be an iterable, not float'). The item cannot be passed by construction.
